CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Add JSON schema for Helm chart values

# GitHub Issue #189: Add JSON schema for Helm chart values

**Category**: improvement | **Scope**: Medium

**Description**: Create a values.schema.json file for the Helm chart that validates all values.yaml fields with proper types, constraints, descriptions, and defaults. Include constraints like minimum replica counts, valid log levels, valid image pull policies, port ranges, and resource request/limit formats. Reference it from Chart.yaml.

**Motivation**: Without a JSON schema, users can set invalid values (e.g., replicas: -1, logLevel: 'verbose') without any feedback until Helm template rendering or runtime failure. A schema provides IDE autocompletion, early validation during helm install/upgrade, and serves as living documentation of all configuration options.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/charts/keystone-operator/`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] values.schema.json covers all fields in values.yaml
- [ ] Schema enforces type constraints, enums for known value sets, and min/max where applicable
- [ ] helm install with invalid values produces a clear validation error
- [ ] IDE autocompletion works with the schema in VS Code with the Helm extension
- [ ] Schema is referenced in Chart.yaml

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/189

User Stories:
- Operator deployer gets early validation of Helm values: As a operator deployer I want Helm to reject invalid values at install/upgrade time before any templ


<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0069): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

<git-identity>
  <rule name="author">ALWAYS use --author flag: git commit --author "Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>" -m "..."</rule>
  <rule name="co-authored-by">Do NOT add any Co-Authored-By trailer. Never add "Co-Authored-By: Claude" or similar.</rule>
  <rule name="trailers">Append these trailers at the end of the commit message body, separated by a blank line:
    AI-assisted: Claude Code
    On-behalf-of: @SAP christian.berendt@sap.com
    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
  </rule>
</git-identity>


<output-format>
OUTPUT ONLY THE COMMIT MESSAGE, nothing else. No markdown formatting.
Body should explain WHAT and WHY (2-4 sentences about what this planning document covers).
</output-format>
